悟.meaning: A quiz champion stares at the last riddle for six hours while her <part>heartbeat</part> races. Suddenly the answer pops into her head like toast. She leaps up and smacks a <part>high five</part> on the startled host's hand. At last she can <kanji>perceive</kanji> what it meant.
悟.on: She pulls off the swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles she wore all night to stay focused.
悟.kun: Her prize: a tin of <sound>sa</sound>rdines, a little <sound>to</sound>tem pole and a tame <sound>roo</sound>k.

努.meaning: A <part>guy</part> at the fair bets he can tow a bus with a rope in his teeth. His face goes red, every <part>muscle</part> shakes, and the bus creeps forward an inch an hour. By sunset it has crossed the car park. He's never worked so hard: a whole day of <kanji>toil</kanji>.
努.on: A <sound>do</sound>lphin in the harbour claps its flippers for him.
努.kun: He sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and leans on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole to rest.

騎.meaning: At the riding show, a <part>horse</part> trots into the ring with something <part>strange</part> on its back: a goldfish in a bowl, wearing a tiny hat. It clears every fence without spilling a drop. The judges give the fish first prize for <kanji>equestrian</kanji> skill.
騎.on: Afterwards the fish reaches into the saddlebag for a tiny <sound>key</sound> and winds up the horse: it was clockwork all along.

凹.meaning: A plump hen likes to nap on top of an upside-down <part>bucket</part>. Every day she's a little heavier, and the metal sags, until there's a cosy dip shaped exactly like her. Now she lays her eggs in it. The bucket's top is <kanji>concave</kanji>.
凹.on: She drags it into the shade of a huge <sound>oa</sound>k, and acorns roll into the dip.
凹.kun: The <sound>he</sound>n shares her dip with a lost <sound>ko</sound>ala.

僚.meaning: At the office trip in the woods, everyone hangs their jackets on one <part>coat hook</part> nailed to a pine and sits round a <part>bonfire</part>. The grumpy man from accounts shares his marshmallows and tells jokes. Out here he isn't the boss's spy; he's your <kanji>colleague</kanji>.
僚.on: Afterwards the whole team sleeps on mats at a quiet <sound>ryo</sound>kan.

裕.meaning: A farmer's <part>weathervane</part> spins to point at the <part>valley</part> whenever good weather is coming. One spring it never stops pointing. Rain at night, sun by day, pumpkins the size of cars. He gives fruit away to every stranger. The harvest is <kanji>abundant</kanji>.
裕.on: A <sound>u</sound>nicorn trots down from the hills to help carry the pumpkins.
